title: Claude solves two open problems in the physics of black holes
lede: Anthropic says agents running Claude Fable 5.2 settled two open questions in theoretical quantum gravity, one about the Hawking-Page transition and one about the modular bootstrap.

points: Claude finished a calculation laid out in 2003 and showed the Hawking-Page phase transition stays abrupt even where spacetime has no definite shape.
For a toy universe with two space dimensions, it found and proved the exact ceiling on the lightest black hole's mass under the simplest bootstrap.
A researcher had Claude pick 22 candidate problems and ran one agent per problem for about six weeks, with agents sharing progress.
The bootstrap method came from an agent working on sphere packing, and the result was formally checked in Lean.
Anthropic says neither result describes our own universe or has practical applications.

points.text: Readers single out the black hole mass ceiling as the more exciting result, though a reply stresses it holds only in a 2D universe.
A physicist cautions that theoretical physics has countless open problems, and most matter to only a handful of specialists.
Some object to crediting Claude in the headline, asking what the prompts were and who framed the problems.
Others note the papers list no human authors at all, only Claude and Anthropic.
